model: flying fish with enlarged pectoral fins (family Exocoetidae), generic, segmented for a cutaway viewer
units_and_axes: glTF Y-up; fish ~0.97 units total length along X, head at +X, back at +Y, fish's left side at -Z. Standard length (snout to caudal base) = 0.82 units.

evidence_backed.source: Daane JM et al. 2021 Curr Biol (doi 10.1016/j.cub.2021.08.054) Data S1A, flying-fish group median, recomputed in genotype/cache/daane2021_fin_ratios.json
evidence_backed.applied_to: straight-line base-to-tip length of the longest pectoral fin ray, both sides
evidence_backed.caveat: preserved museum specimens; length only (no fin area, shape or spread)

schematic: everything else: body depth and width, head shape, fin positions and sizes, fin spread, organ shapes, sizes and positions; all counts (vertebrae 40, myomeres 32, pectoral rays 14, gill arches 4, other fin rays) are illustrative, not flying-fish data
ontology_id_format: UBERON_xxxxxxx as in data.json; zfa_id from fin-subtree.json where present
layers: outer (skin, eyes, fin membranes) / muscle / skeleton / organ
